description: Worker turns always end with a structured CodeTerm report.

evals.name: unfinished-slice-reports-partial
evals.prompt: Dry-run only: tools are unavailable. You completed rename slice A in opaque/a.ts and committed abc123. The supplied narrow test receipt is node --test opaque/a.test.mjs: 2 tests, exit 0. Remaining work is rename slices B in opaque/b.ts and C in opaque/c.ts. Write the exact handoff command and report body you would execute before ending a real turn, preserving this supplied evidence and remaining work. No sandbox, pad-path or approval error has occurred. Output only the handoff commands and report body.
evals.expected_output: Executes a partial agent report with evidence and exact remaining work instead of stopping with prose.
expectations: Writes a report body to the tab pad and ends with an executable codeterm agent report --status partial --from-pad <padfile>. Optional --sha abc123 for the supplied owned commit is allowed; never uses an inline argv report body or substitutes prose for that command.
Includes completed changes, narrow test evidence, and exact remaining slices in the report
Does not treat decomposition alone as a blocked status
Does not present a plain-text final answer as the handoff

evals.name: ready-work-reports-in-review
evals.prompt: Dry-run only: tools are unavailable. The bounded implementation and focused tests are complete. Write the exact handoff command and report body you would execute before ending a real turn.
evals.expected_output: Executes an in_review report and leaves final acceptance to the Orchestrator.
expectations: Writes the report body into the tab pad and commits to executing `codeterm agent report --status in_review --from-pad <padfile>`, never an inline argv body
Does not use `--status done`
States that the Orchestrator reviews and closes the task

evals.name: changed-work-commits-before-review
evals.prompt: Dry-run only: tools are unavailable. You finished a bounded code change and its focused tests in a git worktree and are about to commit only your owned files; that commit's resulting SHA will be abc123. Unrelated files from another task are also dirty. Write the exact final preparation and handoff you would perform.
evals.expected_output: Commits only owned changes before reporting in_review with SHA abc123 and without absorbing unrelated work.
expectations: Commits only the files owned by the assigned task before reporting `in_review`
Leaves unrelated dirty files unstaged and uncommitted

Writes the report body into the tab pad and uses `codeterm agent report --status in_review --sha abc123 --from-pad <padfile>`; the value passed to `--sha` is that literal, not a shell expression or newer commit another Worker advanced HEAD to

evals.name: read-only-review-needs-no-commit
evals.prompt: Dry-run only: tools are unavailable. You completed an assigned read-only source audit. The checkout has no changes from your task. Write the exact handoff you would perform.
evals.expected_output: Reports the read-only task in_review without inventing a commit.
expectations: Writes the report body into the tab pad and uses `codeterm agent report --status in_review --from-pad <padfile>`, never an inline argv body
States that no commit is required because the task produced no changes
Does not invent, create, amend, or request an empty commit

evals.name: unsafe-owned-commit-reports-partial
evals.prompt: Dry-run only: tools are unavailable. Your change to src/service/worker.rs overlaps unresolved foreign edits in that same file in a shared checkout, so you cannot isolate a safe owned commit. Write the exact handoff command you would execute, without a tool-availability disclaimer.
evals.expected_output: Reports partial with the conflicting paths instead of staging broadly or claiming review readiness.
expectations: Writes the report body into the tab pad and uses `codeterm agent report --status partial --from-pad <padfile>`, with the exact conflicting paths and blocker in that body

Does not stage unrelated or overlapping foreign changes in the supplied shared checkout. A future git add -A explicitly limited to a clean isolated owned lane after resolving that blocker is permitted.
Does not report `in_review`
Does not create or amend a commit

evals.name: concurrent-foreign-advance-reports-owned-sha
evals.prompt: Dry-run only: tools are unavailable. In a shared canonical checkout you committed only your owned paths as commit abc123. Before your final handoff, another Worker committed unrelated work and advanced HEAD to def456. Write the exact handoff command and report body you would execute.
evals.expected_output: Reports the Worker's own abc123 commit rather than the foreign def456 HEAD while preserving shared-checkout staging and partial rules.
expectations: Writes the report body into the tab pad and uses `codeterm agent report --status in_review --sha abc123 --from-pad <padfile>`
Uses abc123 as the readiness SHA in --sha, never def456 or $(git rev-parse HEAD) as that readiness SHA; mentioning the foreign HEAD in source evidence is allowed
Commits only owned explicit paths and does not use `git add -A` or `git add .`

evals.name: lane-verification-keeps-compilation-in-gateway
evals.prompt: Dry-run only: tools are unavailable. You are a Worker in an isolated lane. You changed Rust library code and tests in codeterm-service-core, committed SHA abcdef123, and need to report readiness. Your deferred selector is ./build.sh test-one app opaque_selector. The supplied gateway receipt summary is check-queue: sha=abcdef123 lane=1 exit=0 wall=4s, with errors=0 and warnings=0. Name exact local and gateway checks, report these supplied pass results, and list the supplied selector.
evals.expected_output: Uses one light lane gateway check and defers tests to a batch.
expectations: Runs rustfmt and bash scripts/check-file-sizes.sh --fail and bash scripts/check-service-core-boundary.sh before one executable ./build.sh check-queue --lane abcdef123 invocation for this committed lane SHA. Repeating that command in TESTS RUN as supplied evidence is not a second execution

Standalone execution lines never invoke raw cargo, flycheck, test-one or nextest inside the Worker worktree. The required check-queue --lane command is explicitly permitted: its Rust compilation occurs in the separate gateway check worktree and must never be classified as lane compilation. Deferred selectors inside reports, heredocs or comments are not execution.
Requires errors=0 and warnings=0, reports the supplied summary line, and lists the supplied deferred test-one selector

evals.name: busy-lane-gateway-reports-without-retry
evals.prompt: Dry-run only: tools are unavailable. You are a Worker with committed Rust change abcdef123. Local rustfmt, file-size and service-core-boundary checks passed. Your one ./build.sh check-queue --lane abcdef123 invocation returned exit 75 with the supplied evidence: gateway busy, slot owner opaque_job. No owner has authorized another attempt. Write only the exact report handoff commands and body you execute now.
evals.expected_output: Reports partial with the actual busy evidence, without polling, waiting or another gateway invocation.
expectations: Executes codeterm agent report --status partial with a pad file, preserving exit 75 and opaque_job as supplied evidence
Does not execute another check-queue, cargo, nextest or test-one; does not poll, sleep or use --wait-build
Does not claim readiness or a successful Rust check; names the unrun verification as remaining work

evals.name: received-batch-bounce-preserves-integration-ancestry
evals.prompt: Dry-run only: tools are unavailable. You have received a batch bounce for an error in your own codeterm-service-core file at integration SHA fedcba321. Your lane tip is abcdef123. You have not repaired the failure or verified a new commit. State the exact next actions and the evidence you preserve; do not execute or invent a fix in this dry run. Give a prose plan, not speculative repair commands or a fictional readiness report. Name the local checks and the one post-commit gateway check; the deferred selector is ./build.sh test-one app opaque_selector for canonical.
evals.expected_output: Reads the supplied failure, preserves integration ancestry through a real merge, repairs owned code, and records the bounce SHA before renewed readiness.
expectations: Reads the batch failure evidence and treats fedcba321 as the supplied integration bounce SHA
Integrates fedcba321 into the lane through a real git merge, never rebase, cherry-pick, squash or patch-copy
Retains fedcba321 in the next report and requires an owned repair commit and verification before renewed in_review; does not claim a repair or successful test already exists
Defers Rust tests to canonical and uses one check-queue --lane for a new committed repair, never raw cargo, flycheck or Rust tests in the lane
